title: Psychometric Properties Of The Pid-5-Bf In Young Colombian Population: Factor Structure, Reliability, And Invariance By Sex
abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze the psychometric properties of the Personality Inventory for DSM-5 Brief Form (PID-5-BF; 25 items) in a non-clinical young Colombianpopulation. The sample consisted of 1,294 participants aged between 14 and 24 years (M = 18.6, SD = 2.8), of whom 43.1% were men and 56.9% were women. An observational,analytical, and cross-sectional design of an instrumental-psychometric nature was used. Initially, an exploratory factor analysis was performed, showing adequate feasibilityof the matrix (KMO = .904; Bartlett’s test, p < .001) and a five-factor structure that explained 49.6% of the total variance. Subsequently, using confirmatory factor analysiswith WLSMV estimation, the theoretical model of five correlated domains was tested.The fit indices indicated an adequate fit of the model (CFI = .960, TLI = .954, RMSEA = .052, 90% CI [.048, .055], SRMR = .057). Internal consistency was acceptable for the fivedomains (ω = .698–.753; α = .696–.754), with high total reliability (ω = .898; α = .887). Multigroup invariance analysis by sex confirmed configural, metric, scalar, and strictinvariance (CFI ≤ .01), supporting measurement equivalence between men and women.Overall, the results provide evidence of structural validity, internal consistency, and measurement invariance of the PID-5-BF in non-clinical Colombian youth, supporting itsuse in research and comparative studies in this population.
